<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

  /* Reading mode hides the chrome and the empty .arxiv-html-header marker: the pinned JS reads
     the marker's display to know which way to toggle. The marker draws no box. */
  .arxiv-html-header { display: contents; }
  html[data-reading-mode="enabled"] :is(.arxiv-html-site-chrome, .arxiv-html-header, .ds-site-footer) { display: none; }
  /* The paper controls' icons are blocks, so they sit centred (the pinned JS shows the theme
     icon by making its span a block). */
  .arxiv-html-site-chrome .ds-site-header-tools svg { display: block; width: 18px; height: 18px; flex-shrink: 0; fill: currentColor; }
  /* ar5iv dims every image in dark mode and puts it on a white wash, for paper figures;
     arXiv's own render as they are (the logo on the bar, the funder logos on their white
     chips). Important: ar5iv's dark rules are unlayered, as specific as
     :root:not([data-theme]) img:not(.ltx_no_dark_filter). */
  :is(.ds-site-header, .ds-site-footer) img { filter: none !important; }
  .ds-site-header img { background-color: transparent !important; }

  /* Wide (the theme's 1280px): the theme lays the body out as a grid whose full-width top rows
     were the band's and its sticky reader bar's. The band takes the first and scrolls away; the
     header, the paper's bar (no site navigation, the paper's controls), takes the second and
     stays in view, the one sticky bar, with the anchor clearance that requires (DESIGN-POLICIES).
     The controls show their names. */
  @media (min-width: 1280px) {
    html { scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome { display: contents; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > #ds-announcement { grid-area: announce; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > .ds-site-header { grid-area: header; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-icon { display: none; }
  }
  /* Narrow: the header scrolls away, and the controls show icons (names kept for screen
     readers; Why HTML? goes). The theme's contents panel is fixed below where its old sticky
     bar was, and hidden only once the reader has closed it, so until then it is an invisible box
     over the header and the paper: it shows only while open, under the chrome, in its place in
     the page. The paper's footer (build logs, reporting instructions) keeps the text's side
     inset; the theme gives it none, so it met the screen edges. */
  @media (max-width: 1279px) {
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-wide { display: none; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-label { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
    html:not([data-toc-display="block"]) .ltx_page_navbar { display: none; }
    .ltx_page_navbar { position: absolute; top: auto; }
    .arxiv-html-footer { padding-inline: 1rem; }
  }

<span id="id2" class="ltx_text ltx_align_center">Zhan Liu<sup id="id2.1" class="ltx_sup">1,2</sup>, Li Li<sup id="id2.2" class="ltx_sup">1</sup>, Jinchang Xu<sup id="id2.3" class="ltx_sup">1</sup>, Fengyun Rao<sup id="id2.4" class="ltx_sup">1,<sup id="id2.4.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="id2.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">‡</span></sup></sup>, Chao Zhang<sup id="id2.5" class="ltx_sup">2</sup>, Jing LYU<sup id="id2.6" class="ltx_sup">1</sup>

<div class="ltx_dates">November 19, 2026</div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Video understanding, particularly with accompanying audio, remains a central challenge in multimodal intelligence. In this report, we introduce <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">WeMM-Video</span>, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants. Centering on joint audio-visual perception and reasoning, WeMM-Video unifies text, image, audio, and video processing within a hybrid-thinking paradigm, seamlessly supporting both a non-thinking instruct mode for fast, direct responses and a thinking mode for explicit step-by-step reasoning.
The models are trained on a large-scale multimodal corpus of approximately 1.2 trillion tokens through progressive pre-training and a multi-stage post-training pipeline incorporating multi-teacher OPD, anti-repetition MrDPO, and specialist RL.
Evaluated across more than 120 benchmarks, WeMM-Video demonstrates superior performance in omni-modal video understanding and reasoning, while maintaining highly competitive capabilities across general audio, silent video, image, and text tasks. Specifically, in omni-modal video evaluations, our flagship WeMM-Video-35B-A3B establishes a new open-source state of the art, substantially outperforming proprietary models such as Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash and Seed2.0-Mini-0428 while narrowing the gap with the strong Gemini-3.0-Flash, and our compact WeMM-Video-9B surpasses the larger open-source Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct. We publicly release the WeMM-Video family along with our evaluation and reproduction pipeline to foster further research and development in the open-source community.</p>
    
<p id="abstract1.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><a href="https://huggingface.co/collections/tencent/wemm-video" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_align_left ltx_inline-block" style="width:14.8pt;position:relative; bottom:-1.8pt;"><img src="2611.26409v1/figs/hf-icon.png" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:14/13;" width="14" height="13" alt="[Uncaptioned image]"></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">https://huggingface.co/collections/tencent/wemm-video</span></a></p>
    
<p id="abstract1.3" class="ltx_p ltx_align_left"><a href="https://github.com/Tencent/WeMM-Video" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_href" style="font-size:90%;"><span class="ltx_text ltx_align_left ltx_inline-block" style="width:14.8pt;position:relative; bottom:-1.8pt;"><img src="2611.26409v1/figs/github-icon.png" class="ltx_graphics ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:13/13;" width="13" height="13" alt="[Uncaptioned image]"></span><span class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/Tencent/WeMM-Video</span></a></p>
  
</div><span id="footnotex1" class="ltx_note ltx_role_footnotetext"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_outer"><span class="ltx_note_content"><sup class="ltx_note_mark">†</sup><span class="ltx_note_type">footnotetext: </span><sup id="footnotex1.1" class="ltx_sup"><span id="footnotex1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:70%;">∗</span></sup><span id="footnotex1.2" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">Core contributors.

</span></span></span></span>
<figure id="S0.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2611.26409v1/WeMM-Video-capabilities-compact.png" id="S0.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/214;" width="476" height="214" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S0.F1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S0.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">WeMM-Video can perceive and understand omni-modal videos, perform complex multimodal reasoning, and effectively handle general tasks across audio, image, and text modalities.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Video understanding, particularly the unified comprehension of continuous visual scenes and acoustic signals, represents a pivotal frontier in modern multimodal intelligence. Driven by increasingly prevalent real-world scenarios such as short-form video feeds and embodied intelligence, the demand for machines to perceive dynamic audio-visual environments accurately has grown substantially. Building upon rapid advances in large language models (LLMs) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>, <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">90</a>, <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>, <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">104</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>, <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">102</a>, <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">133</a>]</cite>, the multimodal community has witnessed the rise of capable vision-language models <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">53</a>, <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">60</a>, <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">112</a>, <a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">103</a>, <a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>]</cite> and audio LLMs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">98</a>, <a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>, <a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>, <a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">125</a>, <a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">57</a>]</cite>, with pioneering efforts beginning to explore collaborative audio-visual capabilities <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib103" title="" class="ltx_ref">123</a>, <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>, <a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">105</a>, <a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">87</a>, <a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Despite this progress, comprehensively interpreting real-world videos remains a formidable challenge. Beyond recognizing isolated objects, actions, or sounds, an effective model must capture fine-grained temporal dynamics across frames, connect long-range events, and synthesize visual and acoustic cues through deliberate reasoning to grasp both high-level semantics and subtle details. Existing open-source models, however, remain brittle in complex real-world scenarios: they often overlook critical audio-visual details, fail to align acoustic cues with their corresponding visual events, and suffer from cross-modal hallucinations unsupported by video evidence.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To bridge this gap, we introduce and open-source <span id="S1.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">WeMM-Video</span>, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B variants.
Centering on omni-modal video perception and reasoning, WeMM-Video unifies text, image, audio, and video processing within a hybrid-thinking paradigm, supporting both a non-thinking (instruct) mode for low-latency, direct responses and a thinking mode for extended chain-of-thought reasoning. By generating grounded reasoning traces over both visual-only and audio-visual inputs, the thinking mode effectively mitigates cross-modal hallucinations and substantially boosts performance on complex video tasks. To endow the models with these capabilities, we train WeMM-Video on a curated multimodal corpus comprising approximately 1.2 trillion (T) tokens via progressive pre-training, followed by a three-stage post-training pipeline incorporating multi-teacher on-policy distillation (OPD), anti-repetition multi-round direct preference optimization (MrDPO) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">95</a>]</cite>, and specialist reinforcement learning (RL).
Across comprehensive omni-modal video benchmarks, our strongest model, WeMM-Video-35B-A3B, achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance among open-source models of comparable scale and rivals leading proprietary models, including Gemini-3.0-Flash, Seed2.0-Mini-0428 and Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash. WeMM-Video models also maintain strong, well-rounded capabilities across standalone audio, visual-only video, image, and text tasks.
Beyond standard benchmarks, WeMM-Video has been deployed across multiple core video services within WeChat, supporting diverse applications including live-stream commerce, short-form drama analysis, and interactive video scenarios.
Recognizing that standardized evaluation and transparent reproducibility are vital for the open-source community, we release our evaluation and reproduction pipeline alongside the model weights.
We hope the WeMM-Video family can serve as a versatile foundation for community-driven research and real-world applications, pushing the frontiers of open-source omni-modal video understanding.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F2" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.26409v1/wemmvideo.svg" id="S1.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:452/230;" width="452" height="230"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S1.F2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S1.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Model architecture of WeMM-Video.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Model Architecture</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The overall architecture of WeMM-Video primarily draws upon the design of video-SALMONN 2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">95</a>]</cite>, receiving multimodal inputs comprising text, image, audio, and video, and producing textual outputs autoregressively, as illustrated in Fig. <a href="#S1.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 1 Introduction ‣ WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>.
WeMM-Video-2B, WeMM-Video-4B, and WeMM-Video-9B are built on Qwen3.5-2B, Qwen3.5-4B, and Qwen3.5-9B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">81</a>]</cite>, respectively, while WeMM-Video-35B-A3B is built on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">82</a>]</cite>. The audio encoders of WeMM-Video models are initialized from Qwen2.5-Omni <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib103" title="" class="ltx_ref">123</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For visual processing, including both static images and dynamic video frames, we retain the native visual encoders and projection mechanisms of the respective backbones, preserving their pretrained image and video understanding capabilities.
To handle continuous acoustic signals, WeMM-Video incorporates a dedicated audio module comprising a Whisper-based audio encoder <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">83</a>]</cite> and a window-level Q-Former <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">97</a>]</cite>. The Whisper-based encoder extracts acoustic features from audio inputs sampled at 16,000 Hz and segmented into 30-second chunks. The window-level Q-Former then compresses these features within local temporal windows of 0.1 seconds across all model variants, mapping each window to a single audio token in the LLM input space and yielding 10 audio tokens per second. For video inputs with accompanying audio, visual and audio tokens are interleaved in chronological order, supplemented with explicit textual timestamps to facilitate fine-grained cross-modal temporal alignment.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Data</h2>

<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To establish robust multimodal perception and reasoning, WeMM-Video is trained on a comprehensive, high-capacity training corpus. As shown in Fig. <a href="#S3.F3.sf1" title="Figure 3(a) ‣ Figure 3 ‣ 3 Data ‣ WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3(a)</span></a>, the corpus encompasses about 1.2T tokens. Notably, joint audio-visual data constitutes the largest share, contributing 45.4% of the overall volume, providing dense temporal supervision for modeling complex multimodal dynamics.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S3.F3.sf1" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.26409v1/wemm_tokens.svg" id="S3.F3.sf1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_portrait" style="aspect-ratio:318/511;" width="318" height="511"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F3.sf1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(a)</span> </span><span id="S3.F3.sf1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Token distribution by modality.</span></figcaption>
</figure></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2">
<figure id="S3.F3.sf2" class="ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2611.26409v1/wemm_task.svg" id="S3.F3.sf2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/376;" width="476" height="376"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F3.sf2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">(b)</span> </span><span id="S3.F3.sf2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Token distribution by task.</span></figcaption>
</figure></div></div>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S3.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Composition of the WeMM-Video training data.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Besides, Fig. <a href="#S3.F3.sf2" title="Figure 3(b) ‣ Figure 3 ‣ 3 Data ‣ WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3(b)</span></a> illustrates the detailed token distribution across tasks. Captioning accounts for the largest task proportion (37.7%) and serves as the bedrock for foundational multimodal perception. Within this category, we place strategic emphasis on two complementary types of video captions: fine-grained visual captions and joint audio-visual captions. First, for fine-grained visual captioning, we curate an action- and event-dense video split spanning competitive sports, esports, gaming, choreography, and outdoor activities, annotated with dense descriptions that capture rapid physical dynamics and subtle temporal state transitions. Second, for audio-visual captioning, we scale up native omni-modal videos such as films, short-form dramas, interviews, variety shows, and live-stream commerce, synthesizing comprehensive captions that jointly describe visual actions, spoken dialogue, and ambient acoustic signals along a continuous timeline. All candidate captioning data undergo a rigorous pipeline of automated quality scoring, semantic deduplication, and toxicity filtering to ensure both perceptual fidelity and data diversity.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Since the base model natively lacks acoustic perception, we incorporate a dedicated audio corpus to construct and align the acoustic representation space. This collection covers large-scale automatic speech recognition (ASR), music understanding, and general audio understanding.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p4" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond standard single-video streams, real-world applications frequently require models to process streaming feeds and multi-video contexts. To enhance generalization over heterogeneous and complex inputs, we construct a dedicated cross-media understanding split, targeting multi-source tasks such as pairwise video comparison, video-soundtrack compatibility analysis, and e-commerce product-to-ad consistency verification.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p5" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S3.p5.1" class="ltx_p">While perceptual understanding is critical, audio-visual joint reasoning remains a significant bottleneck that existing open-source models rarely address effectively. High-quality knowledge, STEM, and complex reasoning data are indispensable for cultivating these advanced cognitive capabilities; however, verifiable audio-visual reasoning data is naturally scarce in the wild. To bridge this gap, we curate a substantial knowledge and reasoning QA collection via a dual strategy: we incorporate large-scale vision-language STEM and knowledge reasoning datasets augmented with high-quality thinking traces, alongside a curated set of native audio-visual reasoning tasks. This synergy effectively transfers deep reasoning capabilities to omni-modal scenarios while preserving and augmenting the backbone model’s intrinsic problem-solving proficiencies.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Training</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The WeMM-Video family is trained through a unified pipeline comprising progressive multimodal pre-training and multi-stage post-training.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Pre-training</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The pre-training of WeMM-Video follows a progressive three-stage curriculum that systematically expands the context window while enriching cross-modal representations. This strategy smoothly bridges modality gaps, injects broad omni-modal knowledge, and scales long-horizon contextual comprehension, as outlined below.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Stage 1: Acoustic Modality Alignment.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The initial stage focuses on bridging the acoustic representation space with the pre-trained backbone under a compact context window. In this stage, only the audio aligner (i.e., the window-level Q-Former) is optimized, while the backbone LLM and modality encoders remain frozen. Training on foundational audio-text pairs equips the model with core auditory perception capabilities, encompassing ASR and general audio captioning.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Stage 2: Omni-Modal Knowledge Injection.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">With an expanded context window, Stage 2 serves as the core pre-training phase for large-scale omni-modal knowledge injection. Starting from this stage, we unfreeze all model parameters except the visual encoder, as the inherited visual encoder already provides sufficiently strong visual representations. By training on a diverse mixture of textual, visual, auditory, and joint audio-visual data, this stage establishes a unified cross-modal representation space and prepares the model for native omni-modal video comprehension.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Stage 3: Long-Context Capability Scaling.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In the final pre-training stage, we maintain the same trainable parameter configuration as Stage 2 while further scaling the context window to accommodate extended multimodal sequences. Training on lengthy multimodal inputs, such as long-form videos, extended audio recordings, and multi-video scenarios, enhances the model’s capacity to capture long-range temporal dependencies across modalities while preserving robust performance on general downstream tasks.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Post-training</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following large-scale pre-training, the models acquire strong foundational omni-modal capabilities but still face several challenges. First, general language and vision-language capabilities can be further improved, particularly in complex perception and reasoning tasks. Second, generation stability remains a challenge in complex multimodal scenarios, where models may produce excessively long reasoning traces or repetitive outputs. Third, specialized capabilities require further enhancement, especially in challenging tasks such as audio-visual speaker identification, video-soundtrack matching, structured music understanding, and complex audio-visual reasoning. To address these challenges, we develop a progressive three-stage post-training pipeline consisting of multi-teacher OPD, anti-repetition MrDPO, and specialist RL, targeting general capability enhancement, generation stabilization, and specialized capability improvement, respectively.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Multi-Teacher OPD.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We adopt a multi-teacher distillation strategy to enhance general language and vision-language capabilities while preserving omni-modal understanding. Specifically, stronger external teachers provide supervision for text and vision-language tasks to improve general perception and reasoning, while teachers from the same model family are employed to retain existing audio and audio-visual capabilities. We further leverage cross-modal distillation to transfer knowledge from text to audio tasks, enhancing speech understanding and instruction-following. This strategy enables complementary knowledge transfer across modalities while mitigating capability degradation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Anti-Repetition MrDPO.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We observe that the base models have a non-trivial tendency toward repetitive, endless decoding, which persists after pre-training and OPD and hinders subsequent RL training. To address this, we apply MrDPO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">95</a>]</cite> to iteratively optimize the model using offline-mined hard-negative samples exhibiting repetitive decoding across video, audio, and vision-language tasks. Compared with online optimization methods, offline mining more efficiently captures these relatively rare degeneration cases. To maintain stability across multiple optimization rounds, we only update LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite> adapters during each round, merging and reinitializing them between successive rounds.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Specialist RL.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In the final stage, we employ reinforcement learning to enhance challenging downstream capabilities. We curate diverse and challenging training instances through offline inference and evaluation, filtering out samples that the model already solves reliably. Depending on task verifiability, we combine rule-based rewards for deterministic tasks with rubric-based and teacher-consistency rewards for open-ended tasks. A dynamic reward router assigns task-specific rewards, while instruct and thinking modes are jointly optimized through stochastic sampling. We further extend RL to long-context training with increased video frame coverage and sequence lengths, enabling the model to better adapt to extended multimodal inputs and maintain generation stability.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Evaluation</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We conduct comprehensive evaluations of the WeMM-Video family across four core modalities: video, audio, image, and text, covering all four parameter scales: 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For omni-modal video understanding, we compare WeMM-Video against leading proprietary models, including Gemini-3.0-Flash (medium thinking), Seed2.0-Mini-0428 (medium thinking), and Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash, alongside open-source omni-modal models such as Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct and MiniCPM-o-4.5-9B. For silent video understanding, we further include Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B as baselines. Across both video evaluation suites, we report both instruct and thinking mode results for WeMM-Video-35B-A3B to provide a direct comparison with non-thinking baselines and highlight reasoning gains, while reporting only the thinking mode for the 2B, 4B, and 9B variants for conciseness.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For audio understanding, we compare against Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash, Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct, and MiniCPM-o-4.5-9B, evaluating all WeMM-Video variants in instruct mode given the direct perceptual nature of most standard audio benchmarks. For image and text tasks, we compare against Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash, Qwen3.5-9B, and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, and report thinking mode results across all WeMM-Video variants.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1 </span>Omni-Modal Video Evaluation</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 5.1 Omni-Modal Video Evaluation ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.1 Omni-Modal Video Evaluation ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> summarize the performance on joint audio-visual benchmarks. The evaluation is organized around five critical dimensions: general audio-visual understanding, audio-visual hallucination, video-music understanding, audio-visual interaction, and detailed audio-visual captioning. This evaluation suite incorporates 33 representative benchmarks, including Video-MME (with audio) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite>, Video-MME-v2 (with audio) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite>, Daily-Omni <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib58" title="" class="ltx_ref">144</a>]</cite>, WorldSense <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib59" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>]</cite>, AVUT Human <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib60" title="" class="ltx_ref">127</a>]</cite>, AV-SpeakerBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib61" title="" class="ltx_ref">74</a>]</cite>, Video-Holmes <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib62" title="" class="ltx_ref">14</a>]</cite>, OmniVideoBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib63" title="" class="ltx_ref">48</a>]</cite>, RivaBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib64" title="" class="ltx_ref">93</a>]</cite>, LVOmniBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib65" title="" class="ltx_ref">99</a>]</cite>, FutureOmni <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib66" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>, JointAVBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib67" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>, SciVideoBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib68" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>]</cite>, MMOU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib69" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>]</cite>, OmniCompass-AV <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib70" title="" class="ltx_ref">62</a>]</cite>, EvaOmni <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib71" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite>, OmniReasoningBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib96" title="" class="ltx_ref">59</a>]</cite>,
AVHBench Judgement <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib72" title="" class="ltx_ref">94</a>]</cite>, SVHalluc <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib73" title="" class="ltx_ref">135</a>]</cite>, MUSIC-AVQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib74" title="" class="ltx_ref">50</a>]</cite>, HarmonySet <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib75" title="" class="ltx_ref">143</a>]</cite>, Qualcomm IVD <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib77" title="" class="ltx_ref">79</a>]</cite>, OmniVChat <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib76" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>]</cite>, ODU-Bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib78" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>, O-IN-Bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib108" title="" class="ltx_ref">122</a>]</cite>, SocialOmni <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib97" title="" class="ltx_ref">121</a>]</cite>,
Omni-Cloze <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib79" title="" class="ltx_ref">71</a>]</cite>, video-SALMONN 2 testset <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">95</a>]</cite>, UGCVideoCap <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib80" title="" class="ltx_ref">118</a>]</cite>, DVD-Bench (En) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib81" title="" class="ltx_ref">96</a>]</cite>, OmniCap-IF <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib82" title="" class="ltx_ref">109</a>]</cite>, Caption-Based QA on DailyOmni and WorldSense <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib145" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As shown in Table <a href="#S5.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 5.1 Omni-Modal Video Evaluation ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.1 Omni-Modal Video Evaluation ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, our flagship model, WeMM-Video-35B-A3B, establishes a new open-source state of the art in omni-modal video understanding, demonstrating dominance among open-source models while holding a clear advantage over proprietary models such as Seed2.0-Mini-0428 and Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash, and approaching Gemini-3.0-Flash. In general audio-visual understanding, WeMM-Video-35B-A3B (Thinking) surpasses Seed2.0-Mini-0428 on 16 out of 17 benchmarks and also outperforms Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash on 16 out of 17 benchmarks. Beyond general comprehension, WeMM-Video-35B-A3B also performs on par with leading proprietary models across specialized dimensions, including audio-visual hallucination, video-music understanding, audio-visual interaction, and audio-visual captioning. Moreover, WeMM-Video stands out among existing open-source models for its strong native omni-modal thinking capability: as evidenced by comparing the instruct and thinking modes of WeMM-Video-35B-A3B, explicit step-by-step reasoning unlocks substantial performance gains across most audio-visual comprehension and complex reasoning tasks.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Across the smaller variants, the WeMM-Video family similarly delivers strong performance. Notably, WeMM-Video-9B (Thinking) outperforms the leading open-source omni-modal models, Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct and MiniCPM-o-4.5-9B, across most general audio-visual understanding and downstream tasks, while WeMM-Video-4B (Thinking) also surpasses the 30B-scale baseline on the vast majority of benchmarks. Even our most compact WeMM-Video-2B model matches or outperforms the 30B-scale baseline on numerous general perception, hallucination, and captioning benchmarks, offering a highly competitive choice for resource-constrained deployments.</p>
</div>

<li id="S5.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I1.i1.1" class="ltx_sup">1</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">For existing models, we report official results where available and our own evaluations otherwise.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I1.i2.1" class="ltx_sup">2</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">AVHBench results are reported as the sample-wise accuracy across all samples in the judgment tasks.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I1.i3.1" class="ltx_sup">3</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">SVHalluc results are reported as the sample-wise accuracy across all samples.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I1.i4.1" class="ltx_sup">4</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">HarmonySet results are reported as the overall score judged by GPT-4o following official settings.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I1.i5.1" class="ltx_sup">5</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">In audio-visual interaction evaluation, O-IN-Bench is evaluated with GPT-6-Luna as the judge following official settings, and the other benchmarks with GPT-6.1-Sol.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I1.i6.1" class="ltx_sup">6</sup></span>

</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I1.i7.1" class="ltx_sup">7</sup></span>

</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i8" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I1.i8.1" class="ltx_sup">8</sup></span>

</div></li>
<li id="S5.I1.i9" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I1.i9.1" class="ltx_sup">9</sup></span>

<li id="S5.I1.i10" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I1.i10.1" class="ltx_sup">10</sup></span>

<li id="S5.I3.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I3.i1.1" class="ltx_sup">1</sup></span>

<p id="S5.I3.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">For existing models, we report official results where available and our own evaluations otherwise.</span></p>

<p id="S5.I3.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Video-IFBench results are reported as TCSR | TISR.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I3.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I3.i3.1" class="ltx_sup">3</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I3.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I3.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">VidHalluc results are reported as the average score across the four subtasks: BQA, MCQ, TSH, and STH.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I3.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I3.i4.1" class="ltx_sup">4</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I3.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I3.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">MMBench-Video scores are reported on a scale of 0–3.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I3.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I3.i5.1" class="ltx_sup">5</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I3.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I3.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">TemporalBench results are reported using the overall MBA score.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I3.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I3.i6.1" class="ltx_sup">6</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I3.i6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I3.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">F-16-NBA is reported as accuracy.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I3.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I3.i7.1" class="ltx_sup">7</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I3.i7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I3.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I3.i7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">TimeLens results are reported as mean IoU.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div></div></div>
</figure>

<div id="S5.T4.6" class="ltx_block ltx_figure_panel ltx_minipage ltx_align_center ltx_align_middle" style="width:345.0pt;">
<ol id="S5.I4" class="ltx_enumerate" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.5em;">
<li id="S5.I4.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I4.i1.1" class="ltx_sup">1</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I4.i1.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I4.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I4.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">For existing models, we report official results where available and our own evaluations otherwise.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I4.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I4.i2.1" class="ltx_sup">2</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I4.i2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I4.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I4.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Video-IFBench results are reported as TCSR | TISR.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I4.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I4.i3.1" class="ltx_sup">3</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I4.i3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I4.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I4.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">VidHalluc results are reported as the average score across the four subtasks: BQA, MCQ, TSH, and STH.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I4.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I4.i4.1" class="ltx_sup">4</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I4.i4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I4.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I4.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">MMBench-Video scores are reported on a scale of 0–3.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I4.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I4.i5.1" class="ltx_sup">5</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I4.i5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I4.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I4.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">TemporalBench results are reported using the overall MBA score.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I4.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I4.i6.1" class="ltx_sup">6</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I4.i6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I4.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I4.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">F-16-NBA is reported as accuracy.</span></p>
</div></li>
<li id="S5.I4.i7" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I4.i7.1" class="ltx_sup">7</sup></span> 
<div id="S5.I4.i7.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.I4.i7.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I4.i7.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">TimeLens results are reported as mean IoU.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div></div></div>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 5.2 Silent Video Evaluation ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> and Table <a href="#S5.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 5.2 Silent Video Evaluation ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> present the evaluation results on silent video benchmarks. We evaluate the models across seven core dimensions: general video understanding, long video understanding, fine-grained perception, temporal grounding, spatial understanding, streaming video understanding, and multi-video understanding. The evaluation suite encompasses 32 established benchmarks, including Video-MME <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite>, Video-MME-v2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">27</a>]</cite>, MVBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">54</a>]</cite>, Video-MMMU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>]</cite>, MME-VideoOCR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">89</a>]</cite>, TempCompass <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">64</a>]</cite>, NExT-QA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">120</a>]</cite>, TOMATO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">88</a>]</cite>, Video-IFBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">61</a>]</cite>, VidHalluc <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib39" title="" class="ltx_ref">49</a>]</cite>, VideoVista <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib40" title="" class="ltx_ref">56</a>]</cite>, MMVU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">138</a>]</cite>, Video-Index <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib42" title="" class="ltx_ref">91</a>]</cite>, Perception Test <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib43" title="" class="ltx_ref">78</a>]</cite>, TimeBlind <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib98" title="" class="ltx_ref">47</a>]</cite>, Video-MME-Logical <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib99" title="" class="ltx_ref">45</a>]</cite>, MLVU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib44" title="" class="ltx_ref">141</a>]</cite>, LVBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib45" title="" class="ltx_ref">111</a>]</cite>, LongVideoBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib46" title="" class="ltx_ref">117</a>]</cite>, EgoSchema <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib55" title="" class="ltx_ref">72</a>]</cite>, MMBench-Video <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib47" title="" class="ltx_ref">25</a>]</cite>, MotionBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib48" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>, TemporalBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib49" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>, F-16-NBA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib50" title="" class="ltx_ref">55</a>]</cite>, TimeLens <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib51" title="" class="ltx_ref">136</a>]</cite>, PAI-Bench-U <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib52" title="" class="ltx_ref">139</a>]</cite>, MMSI-Video-Bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib53" title="" class="ltx_ref">58</a>]</cite>, VSI-Bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib54" title="" class="ltx_ref">126</a>]</cite>, OVO-Bench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib56" title="" class="ltx_ref">75</a>]</cite>, CrossVid <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib57" title="" class="ltx_ref">52</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Overall, the WeMM-Video family demonstrates highly competitive performance on silent video understanding without suffering much from the visual degradation often introduced by acoustic modality integration. In particular, WeMM-Video-35B-A3B holds a clear lead over Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash across nearly all benchmarks, while performing on par with its strong vision-language backbone, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, as well as the proprietary Seed2.0-Mini-0428 across evaluated dimensions. Consistent trends are observed across the smaller variants: WeMM-Video-9B and WeMM-Video-4B substantially outperform the open-source omni-modal baselines Qwen3-Omni-30B-A3B-Instruct and MiniCPM-o-4.5-9B, with WeMM-Video-9B matching or surpassing its Qwen3.5-9B backbone on the majority of benchmarks and WeMM-Video-2B delivering competitive results at a compact scale.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Audio Evaluation</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 5.3 Audio Evaluation ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> summarizes the evaluation results on standalone audio benchmarks across five core dimensions: general audio understanding, music understanding, speech recognition, lyrics recognition, and voice interaction. The evaluation suite encompasses 18 established benchmarks, including MMAU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib83" title="" class="ltx_ref">86</a>]</cite>, MMAU-Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib84" title="" class="ltx_ref">44</a>]</cite>, MMAR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib85" title="" class="ltx_ref">70</a>]</cite>, MMSU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib86" title="" class="ltx_ref">108</a>]</cite>, DCase 2025 AQA (dev subset) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib87" title="" class="ltx_ref">124</a>]</cite>,
RUL-MuchoMusic <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib88" title="" class="ltx_ref">132</a>]</cite>,
HumMusQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib143" title="" class="ltx_ref">116</a>]</cite>, MusTBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib144" title="" class="ltx_ref">46</a>]</cite>,
GigaSpeech <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib89" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>, VoxPopuli <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib90" title="" class="ltx_ref">107</a>]</cite>, LibriSpeech <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib91" title="" class="ltx_ref">77</a>]</cite>, WenetSpeech <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib92" title="" class="ltx_ref">134</a>]</cite>, MIR-1K <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib93" title="" class="ltx_ref">38</a>]</cite>, Opencpop <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib94" title="" class="ltx_ref">113</a>]</cite>, VoiceBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib95" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite>, IFEval-Audio <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib100" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite>, Speech-IFEval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib101" title="" class="ltx_ref">66</a>]</cite>,
and Audio MultiChallenge <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib102" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>

<ol id="S5.I5" class="ltx_enumerate" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:1.5em;">

</div></li>
<li id="S5.I5.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I5.i3.1" class="ltx_sup">3</sup></span>

</div></li>
<li id="S5.I5.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><sup id="S5.I5.i4.1" class="ltx_sup">4</sup></span>

<p id="S5.I5.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I5.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">MIR-1K and Opencpop results are reported as CER.</span></p>

<div id="S5.I5.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.I5.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S5.I5.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Audio MultiChallenge results are reported as the average pass rate.</span></p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div></div></div>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Although primarily centered on video understanding, the WeMM-Video family exhibits strong, well-rounded audio capabilities. Notably, WeMM-Video excels in general audio understanding. The 35B-A3B variant surpasses open-source baselines across widely used benchmarks like MMAU-Pro, MMAR, and MMSU, and performs on par with the proprietary Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash. Moreover, benefiting from targeted optimization, WeMM-Video leads on voice interaction and spoken instruction-following benchmarks, while also remaining highly competitive in music understanding as well as speech and lyrics recognition.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.4 </span>Image Evaluation</h3>

<div id="S5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T6" title="Table 6 ‣ 5.4 Image Evaluation ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> presents the evaluation results on static image benchmarks across seven core dimensions: STEM and puzzle reasoning, general VQA, text and document understanding, spatial understanding, multi-image understanding, object counting, and multimodal instruction following. The evaluation suite encompasses 28 established benchmarks, including MMMU <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib104" title="" class="ltx_ref">130</a>]</cite>, MMMU-Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib105" title="" class="ltx_ref">131</a>]</cite>, MathVision <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib106" title="" class="ltx_ref">110</a>]</cite>, MathVista <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib107" title="" class="ltx_ref">67</a>]</cite>, DynaMath <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib109" title="" class="ltx_ref">145</a>]</cite>, ZEROBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib110" title="" class="ltx_ref">85</a>]</cite>, ZEROBench_sub <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib110" title="" class="ltx_ref">85</a>]</cite>, VisualPuzzles <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib111" title="" class="ltx_ref">92</a>]</cite>, RealWorldQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib114" title="" class="ltx_ref">119</a>]</cite>, MMStar <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib112" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>]</cite>, MMBench<math id="S5.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="{}_{\text{EN-DEV-v1.1}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow></mrow><mtext>EN-DEV-v1.1</mtext></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">{}_{\text{EN-DEV-v1.1}}</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite </figure>
<div id="S5.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Overall, the WeMM-Video family effectively preserves the strong image perception and reasoning capabilities of its vision-language backbones from omni-modal training. Specifically, WeMM-Video-35B-A3B and WeMM-Video-9B comprehensively outperform Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash across nearly all evaluated benchmarks, while performing on par with their respective Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-9B backbones.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.5 </span>Text Evaluation</h3>

<div id="S5.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T7" title="Table 7 ‣ 5.5 Text Evaluation ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ WeMM-Video: Pushing the Frontiers of Open-Source Omni-Modal Video Understanding" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a> presents the evaluation results on pure text benchmarks across five core dimensions: general knowledge, instruction following, long-context understanding, STEM problem solving, and mathematical reasoning. The evaluation suite encompasses 12 established benchmarks, including MMLU-Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib131" title="" class="ltx_ref">114</a>]</cite>, MMLU-Redux <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib132" title="" class="ltx_ref">29</a>]</cite>, SuperGPQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib133" title="" class="ltx_ref">24</a>]</cite>, C-Eval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib134" title="" class="ltx_ref">42</a>]</cite>, IFEval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib135" title="" class="ltx_ref">140</a>]</cite>, IFBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib136" title="" class="ltx_ref">80</a>]</cite>, CFBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib137" title="" class="ltx_ref">137</a>]</cite>, AA-LCR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib138" title="" class="ltx_ref">100</a>]</cite>, LongBench v2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib139" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite>, GPQA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib140" title="" class="ltx_ref">84</a>]</cite>, HMMT Nov 25 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib141" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>]</cite>, and IMOAnswerBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib142" title="" class="ltx_ref">68</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T7" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T7.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Table 7</span>: </span><span id="S5.T7.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Evaluation results of the WeMM-Video family and baselines on pure text benchmarks. Best results are in bold.</span></figcaption>
<div id="S5.T7.5" class="ltx_inline-block ltx_align_center ltx_transformed_outer" style="width:345.0pt;height:120.2pt;vertical-align:-58.8pt;"><span class="ltx_transformed_inner" style="transform:translate(-161.5pt,56.3pt) scale(0.516463632848199,0.516463632848199) ;">
<table id="S5.T7.5.1" class="ltx_tabular ltx_guessed_headers ltx_align_middle">
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">
<tr id="S5.T7.5.1.1" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S5.T7.5.1.1.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_tt" rowspan="2"><span id="S5.T7.5.1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Benchmark</span></th>
<td id="S5.T7.5.1.1.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt"><span id="S5.T7.5.1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Qwen3.5-Omni-</span></td>

</figure>
<div id="S5.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S5.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Consistent with the image evaluation findings, incorporating audio-visual modalities into WeMM-Video preserves the core linguistic capabilities of the base models. Across all evaluated dimensions, WeMM-Video-35B-A3B and WeMM-Video-9B substantially outperform Qwen3.5-Omni-Flash, while performing on par with their respective Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and Qwen3.5-9B backbones and achieving further improvements in instruction following.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para ltx_noindent">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this report, we present WeMM-Video, a family of Chinese-English bilingual omni-modal foundation models spanning 2B, 4B, 9B, and 35B-A3B parameter scales. Centered on omni-modal video understanding and reasoning, WeMM-Video unifies text, image, audio, and video processing within a hybrid-thinking paradigm through progressive three-stage pre-training and a multi-stage post-training pipeline comprising multi-teacher OPD, anti-repetition MrDPO, and specialist RL. Comprehensive evaluations demonstrate that our flagship WeMM-Video-35B-A3B establishes a new open-source state of the art in omni-modal video understanding and rivals leading proprietary models, while our lightweight variants exhibit strong cross-scale efficiency. Beyond joint audio-visual comprehension, the WeMM-Video family also delivers leading performance across audio, silent video, image, and text modalities. We publicly release the model weights along with the complete evaluation and reproduction pipeline, and we hope WeMM-Video will serve as a solid foundation for future research and real-world omni-modal applications.</p>
</div>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
</section>

      all.</p>
